beats.visual_focus: A high-speed GPU utilization bar dropping to near zero repeatedly during inference.

beats.text: The villain is the target model, acting like a relay runner who stops to check their shoelaces after every single step of the race.
beats.visual_focus: A runner sprinting, then abruptly stopping, then sprinting again, repeating endlessly.

beats.text: Enter DLoop: a looped architecture that forces the draft model to keep sprinting, stacking multiple drafts before the target model finally intervenes.
beats.visual_focus: A chain of draft tokens stacking up in a buffer before a single verification pulse hits.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook is solid—calling out H100 idle time immediately caught my attention because that's actual pain for anyone running inference. The relay runner analogy in Beat 2 was actually decent and didn't feel like 'baby talk.' I got the gist of the mechanism, but 'loop-aware training' sounds like a buzzword unless you briefly explain that it's just modifying the loss function to account for the draft model's recursive inputs.
